children.text: Coron, on Busuanga Island in northern Palawan, is famous for Kayangan Lake and Barracuda Lake tucked inside limestone islands, and Twin Lagoon. Japanese warships sunk during World War II form a world-class wreck-diving destination, and there's also Mount Tapyas viewpoint and a seawater hot spring to enjoy.

Coron is a city in the Calamian Islands north of the main Palawan island. What travelers call "Coron" usually refers to Coron town at the southeastern end of Busuanga Island, Coron Island just offshore, and the surrounding islands all together. Coron Island, the center of the trip, is covered in sharp limestone peaks, with around ten hidden lakes inside the island and lagoons ringed by cliffs along the coast.

Coron Island is the ancestral territory of the indigenous Tagbanwa people, formally recognized by the Philippine government as their ancestral domain. So major sites like Kayangan Lake, Barracuda Lake, and Twin Lagoon are managed directly by the Tagbanwa community, which charges entrance fees and sets swimming zones and visiting hours. Most of the island's lakes are considered sacred sites and are off-limits to visitors.
Coron has another face beneath the waves. On
September 24, 1944

, a Japanese fleet hiding in Coron Bay was attacked by US Navy carrier aircraft, sinking over ten ships at once, including supply ships and a seaplane tender. The wrecks of the seaplane tender Akitsushima, the supply ship Irako, and the tanker Okikawa Maru remain relatively intact at depths of
, making Coron one of the world's top ten wreck-diving destinations. Even without diving, you can see the Skeleton Wreck in shallow water by snorkeling.

Where El Nido centers on beaches and lagoons, Coron offers a wider range of experiences — lakes, wrecks, viewpoints, and hot springs. It especially suits divers, snorkeling enthusiasts, and travelers after dramatic scenic photos.
Coron town covers about 689 km² and has a population of roughly 70,000 (69,439 as of 2024), divided into 23 barangays. On
June 5, 1998
, Coron Island was officially recognized as the Tagbanwa people's ancestral domain, and after holding rituals, the community opened Kayangan Lake and Barracuda Lake to tourists from
. Siete Pecados Marine Park in Coron Bay received the Blue Park Award in
April 2024
. Kayangan Lake is only a little over
10 minutes

by boat from the Coron town pier, and the other lakes and the wreck-diving waters can also be reached and returned from within half a day, so the usual approach is to stay in Coron town and head out by boat each day.
The highlight of the Coron Island tour: climb the steps for about
10–15 minutes

to a viewpoint overlooking the bay between limestone peaks, then descend to the clear lake on the other side to swim. A queue forms for photos at the viewpoint, so it's best to go early. The lake is brackish, with fresh water and seawater mixed at roughly 7 to 3, and its depth reaches about
at most. Since a freediving accident in
, wearing a life jacket has been mandatory.
A remarkable lake where fresh water and seawater form layers and the temperature changes sharply with depth. It is also known as a freediving and diving spot. The depth is about
or more, and the surface water is a cool
, but the deeper layers are heated like hot spring water, in the high 30s ℃. The entrance fee is about
and is often not included in tour prices; individual visits are not possible, and you can only go by island tour boat.
Swim through a narrow gap in the rocks, or cross a ladder, and a second lagoon appears. You can swim across at low tide, and use the ladder at high tide.
Diving to explore the remains of World War II Japanese vessels such as the Akitsushima, Irako, and Okikawa Maru. Diving inside the hulls is only for experienced divers with wreck-diving training.

blocks.title: Snorkeling the Skeleton Wreck and coral gardens

children.text: With shallow water letting you see the wreck's skeleton even from the surface, the Skeleton Wreck and coral gardens are recommended for non-divers.
Climb the more than 700 steps up the mountain behind Coron town and watch the sun set over the sea and islands beside a large cross. The climb takes about
20–30 minutes
. There is no separate admission fee, though a small amount is sometimes collected at the foot of the steps, and it's best to start climbing
1 hour–1 hour 30 minutes
before sunset.
A seawater hot spring bubbling up beside coastal mangroves, where you can soak away the day's fatigue in warm water of about 38–40℃. Going after sunset is noticeably cooler. The entrance fee is about
(adult and child rates differ), and opening hours are generally

Direct flights operate to Busuanga Airport (USU, Francisco B. Reyes Airport) from Clark, Cebu, and El Nido. From Clark it takes about
1 hour
and costs about
one way. The airport is about
40 minutes
by car from Coron town, and a shared van from in front of the airport costs about
per person and drops you off at your lodging.
Since
March 29, 2026

, propeller aircraft have been banned from Manila's Ninoy Aquino Airport, so there are no direct Manila–Busuanga flights. If departing from Manila, either take the P2P bus from NAIA Terminal 3, PITX, and elsewhere to Clark Airport (about
2 hours 30 minutes–3 hours
, about

Busuanga Airport (Francisco B. Reyes Airport, USU) is a small airport with a runway about

long, so it is served mainly by turboprops such as the ATR. The airlines flying here are Cebgo (Clark, Cebu, El Nido), PAL Express (Cebu, Clark), and Sunlight Air (Cebu, Clark); the Clark and Cebu routes take about
1 hour 20 minutes
, and the El Nido route about
30–40 minutes
. Cebu–Coron is flown by PAL almost daily, making it the easiest connection. Flight schedules change with the season, so check the timetable when you book.
Fast ferries operated by Montenegro Lines, Pimal Fast Ferry, Atienza Inter-Island, Jomalia, and others run daily between El Nido and Coron. They usually depart between
6 and 8 AM
, take about
3 hours 30 minutes–5 hours
, and cost about

depending on the operator and seat class. In peak season it is safest to book one to two weeks ahead. From Manila, a large 2GO passenger ship sails one to two times a week (a schedule departing Friday evening and arriving the next morning is known), taking about
13–16 hours
and costing about
depending on cabin class, but operators and schedules change often, so check the latest timetable. Cancellations are frequent in the rough-sea months of
November–February
Get around Coron town by tricycle (about

for a ride in town, negotiable for a charter). The Maquinit Hot Spring and the trailhead for Mount Tapyas are an easy tricycle ride away. Island tours mostly run as join tours with hotel pickup included, and motorbike rental costs about
per day.
Island tours leave from the Coron town pier by bangka boat. The Kayangan Lake landing is a little over
10 minutes
away, and the Coron Island tour usually starts at
and ends around
. Many join tours are packages that include lake entrance fees and lunch, while private boats charge per boat. Booking by the day before is often enough, but in peak season the spots fill up quickly.
There are currently no direct flights between Puerto Princesa and Coron; a 2GO passenger ship sails once a week and takes about
12–13 hours
. The two cities are on different islands and are not connected by road, so most people go via El Nido or fly from Manila or Clark. Check the operator's notices for the timetable.
November
through
May
is the dry season and good for travel.
March
through
May

especially has the calmest sea and best visibility, ideal conditions for both lake swimming and wreck diving. During Holy Week and summer break, popular sites get crowded, so an early start is recommended.
From
December
to
February

, the northeast monsoon Amihan brings windy days that can cancel far-island tours or the El Nido ferry. Still, the area right around Coron Island is sheltered by surrounding islands, so tours run on many days.
From
June
to
October
is the rainy and typhoon season. As with Typhoon Haiyan (Yolanda), which struck Coron in
, a strong typhoon can pass through, making forecast checks essential. Even in the rainy season, mornings are often clear, and wreck diving is possible nearly year-round, though visibility can drop.
Coron's average annual rainfall is about 2,500 mm, and at its hottest the temperature climbs to
. The peak season is
December–March
, and
June–September
is the low season, when tour and lodging prices drop but the weather is much less predictable. The town fiesta honoring Coron's patron saint, Saint Augustine, is on
August 28

Coron town's center is the most convenient place to stay, with a cluster of guesthouses and mid-range hotels (about
per night), close to tour pickups and restaurants. For sea views, resorts on the outskirts hills or the coast (about
per night) are good. For a quiet island getaway, an island resort around Busuanga is an option, though it requires boat transport and costs more.

Coron town has many seafood restaurants. It's popular to pick fresh fish, shrimp, squid, and crab and have them grilled or cooked in chili sauce; Coron specialties include cashews (Palawan is a cashew-growing region) and seafood dishes. Cheap restaurants near the public market serve Filipino home cooking for about
per person. Island tour lunches usually feature grilled fish, pork barbecue, rice, and fruit.
Lodging prices run about
for a dorm bed, about
for a guesthouse, about
for a mid-range hotel, and about
for a boutique resort on the Coron Bay side, while luxury resorts on Busuanga Island cost
or more. Rooms fill up early in peak season, so it's best to book together with your flights.

Local dishes worth trying in Coron include kilawin, fresh-caught fish cured in coconut vinegar, ginger, and chili, and tamilok, a mollusk that lives in mangrove logs, eaten raw dressed in vinegar and calamansi. Among the seafood restaurants, Lobster King is known for letting you pick fresh fish and live lobsters from the display and have them cooked right away, and Kawayanan Grill Station is known for its grilled dishes. Opinions on both are mixed, so it's best to check the price list and weights first. Restaurants around the public market serve a meal for about
, and souvenir shops around town sell cashew products as gifts.
Town has a few ATMs, but cash often runs out on weekends and in peak season. It's best to bring enough cash before you arrive.
Site entrance fees are often not included in tour prices, so confirm this when booking.
Popular tours crowd Kayangan Lake at
. Reversing the tour order or requesting an early departure gives a much more relaxed visit.
The steps at Kayangan Lake are steep and slippery, so sturdy-soled shoes are better than aqua shoes or sandals.
Before wreck diving, tell the dive center exactly your certification level and depth limit.
Vans to the airport are often scheduled well over
2 hours
before your flight, so it's best to confirm the pickup time in advance.
Smart and Globe signals are good in town but drop out almost entirely during island tours.
Kayangan Lake can be entered only between
7 AM and 4 PM
, and the admission fee of about
includes a life jacket and a local guide. If you arrive at
just after opening, you will barely have to queue at the viewpoint.
The Coron environmental fee is about

, paid on arrival at the airport or port, and is reported to be valid for 10 days once paid. Where and how much you pay may change, so check the latest notices, and keep the receipt so you can show it on tours.

You often get wet on tour boats, so bring a waterproof case or dry bag. The ATMs in Coron town (BPI and Landbank) can run out of cash on weekends and in peak season, so it's best to prepare small change in advance for the environmental fee and entrance fees.

Coron Island's lakes and lagoons are sacred Tagbanwa territory. Swimming outside designated zones, noise, and littering are banned, and rules and fees can change by community decision, so check the latest notices.
Wreck interiors are dangerous due to their maze-like structure and silt, so divers without the proper training should never enter.
Wearing a life jacket is mandatory at Kayangan Lake, and at Barracuda Lake and other places you must wear one if you are not a confident swimmer.
The limestone rocks are sharp and easy to cut your feet on, so wearing aqua shoes is a good idea.
Tours and ferries can be cancelled suddenly during typhoon and monsoon season, so leave buffer time in your schedule.
You must not fly within
24 hours
of diving.
In
November 2025

, Typhoon Tino (international name Kalmaegi) caused flooding and road cutoffs in northern Palawan, including Coron, Busuanga, and El Nido. During the rainy and typhoon season, tours, ferries, and flights can be suspended suddenly, so leave buffer time in your schedule and check weather forecasts.
